case_quality.notes: Genuine teeth, but what it pins is narrower than the design's L07. It survives M1b (status gate removed from candidate collection) - i.e. yes, it would still pass if the resolver ignored the row's status: the vacated row has no file so the local probe skips it and the verified new row is served with identical document/hash fields, and the `canonical_location_id` assertion compares against the SERVED row (resolver._handle builds the handle from _select_candidate's pick), so it stays true. The 'reference unchanged' half is structurally weak because source_id (and therefore document_id) is a pure function of the content hash (source_manifest.py:249) - a byte-identical move cannot change it; the locator machinery is the real subject. Does it exercise a NEW location row? Yes: measured 4 rows (old PDF+sidecar missing, new PDF+sidecar active) with new location_ids. Does it depend on incidental behaviour (the sidecar moving too)? Yes, and this is a coverage limit: moving the PDF alone leaves the moved file `active` but reclassifies the document group, so document_kind drops out of the annual_report slice and the answer is MISSING with an EMPTY trace (a second, orphan-sidecar document row is source_status='incomplete'). The case's docstring says 'both the PDF and its sidecar', but neither the acceptance nor the evidence registers the paired-move precondition or the silent empty-trace failure.

Isolating the two mechanisms: (a) with the request as written, the other revision is rejected at `provider_document_id_not_strong` before any location logic runs; (b) with the provider pin removed from the request, the other revision IS served, as reused_equivalent; (c) if the surviving revision declares the same provider id, it is served as reused_exact with its own bytes. So the case pins 'another DOCUMENT is not substituted for a provider-pinned request', which is a real guarantee, but the evidence attributes it to the wrong mechanism. Minor: the final assertion (`not any(OTHER_DIGEST == match.content_sha256 ...)`) is vacuous after `after.matches == ()`; the useful part of that block is the check that the other revision's row really is active.

findings.claim: F-B04-1's consequence statement overstates the loss and mis-attributes its cause: findings.md F-B04-1 (and progress.md:7, checkpoint.json:5, b04-implementation.md section 3) say the re-point makes the superseded revision's reference '不可再解引用' / 'no longer dereferenceable'.
findings.evidence: Measured in an isolated copy: (a) after the overwrite, reader.resolve_handle(superseded_document_id, expected_content_sha256=old_sha) STILL returns the record (document_id, content_sha256=2a12f260634f, source_status='active') and returns None for a wrong hash - that API reads documents/sources and never consults `locations`; (b) the superseded `documents` row survives with its original primary_source_id, so the catalog still holds the reference record; (c) no file under the fixture carries the old sha any more - the bytes were destroyed by the in-place overwrite, not by the upsert; (d) with a second copy (another path or another root) the old reference resolves reused_exact with the correct bytes. So what is actually lost is the active locator plus the bytes, and the reuse path answers MISSING/download_required=true.
findings.impact: The step's central finding, which the owner will use to choose a remedy, describes a different failure than the measured one (locator bookkeeping rather than 'no byte snapshot exists'). A reader would conclude the catalog lost the ability to dereference a reference it in fact still answers at document level, and would look for the defect in the write face's upsert rather than in the absence of a byte snapshot.
findings.required_action: Restate F-B04-1 as three precise statements: (1) the in-place overwrite destroys the only copy of the superseded revision's bytes (no file carries the old sha); (2) the superseded revision loses every active location row, so the reuse path answers MISSING with download_required=true and trace no_canonical_active_location; (3) the document/source record survives and reader.resolve_handle(document_id, expected_content_sha256=...) still dereferences the reference record (fail-closed on hash drift). Scope the phrase '引用不可再解引用' to the reuse/locator path.

findings.claim: findings.md F-B04-1 item 2 and progress.md:7 state, without qualification, that the superseded revision '不再有任何 active location' (has no active location left).
findings.evidence: Measured counter-example: keeping a second copy of the old revision either at another path in the same root (backup/2025.pdf) or under a second registered root, then overwriting the first path with a new revision, leaves the superseded document with active locations and the old reference resolves reused_exact with the correct sha 2a12f260634f, served from the surviving copy. Only when the overwritten path held the ONLY copy does the document end up with zero location rows.

findings.claim: F-B04-1's three candidate remedies are listed without saying which one restores what, and the commit message's summary 'three candidate remedies, all of which touch the write face or the DDL' is false for one of them.
findings.evidence: findings.md:13 lists (i) keep the old row marked moved/superseded (DDL/write path), (ii) a controlled snapshot by the canonical writer, (iii) accept 'same-path overwrite loses the old reference' in the contract. Remedy (i) alone cannot restore dereferenceability: after the overwrite there are no old bytes to point at (measured: no file carries the old sha), so it only records the fact. Remedy (iii) touches neither the write face nor the DDL (commit-message claim false). Also unrecorded: an in-scope alternative exists in the allowed F2 file - the resolver currently reports `no_canonical_active_location` both for 'this document has no location rows at all' (the F-B04-1 case) and for 'a location exists but is not qualified'; a trace refinement distinguishing them is possible with no behavioural change (not attempted here).
findings.impact: The owner could approve remedy (i) expecting the old reference to work again, and the finding's blanket 'all remedies are out of scope' hides a cheap in-scope diagnostic option that was neither implemented nor explicitly rejected.
findings.required_action: Label each remedy with what it restores (ii = bytes; i = audit trail/supersession record only; iii = acceptance only), fix the commit-message claim in the run records that repeat it, and record the F2 trace refinement as considered-and-rejected (with the reason: the trace string is asserted by the pinned case and no behaviour changes) or schedule it.

no_product_change_verdict: Defensible as a code decision, not defensible as worded. The design's goals 1-2 held after B02 and are now accepted (a move keeps the reference; a provider-pinned request is not served another revision). Goal 3 - 'the old reference remains dereferenceable' after a same-path overwrite (b-design.md section B04:148, explicitly assigned to this step) - does not hold, and no in-scope change can make it hold: the old bytes are physically destroyed by the overwrite (measured: no file carries the old sha), and the re-point is scanner.py:1123-1124 against the locations DDL unique index (root_id, relative_path) in store.py - scanner.py (allowed only for :1007-1099), store.py and canonical_writer.py are all outside the allowed set (file-scope v0.1.7 sections 1-2), so 'refusing to re-point' is impossible from F1/F2, and serving the old revision from another surviving copy already works without any change (measured). B04 is therefore a legitimate verification-only step for goals 1-2, plus a correct escalation of goal 3 - but the sentence 'the design goal already held after B02' is false for goal 3 (B-VR04-03), the finding's consequence statement overstates the loss (B-VR04-01), and the finding has no scheduled work-package slot: task_plan.md:26 and checkpoint.json register it as a note ('登记独立工作包') with no step id, while the owner still owes a ruling on whether to fund remedy (ii) (a byte snapshot on the write face) or remedy (iii) (a contract-level known limitation). Recommended: keep 'no product change', fix the four status texts, correct F-B04-1 as in B-VR04-01/-05, and add the F-B04-1 owner decision to the pending-rulings list alongside S-10/S-11.
limitations: No access to the real multi-root production catalog, to real filing bytes, or to an isolated copy of them (gate G8 is not available to me): every fixture was synthetic PDF+sidecar material in %TEMP%, i.e. the protocol's L1 mechanism layer only. The L2 real-byte layer and the R1 layers of b-vr-protocol.md section 2 were not exercised, and the F-B04-1 scenario was not replayed against real production layout (e.g. a real 10-K amendment overwriting the same path).

The consumer side (filing-fetch / revenue-forecast callers) was not inspected: whether every production request pins provider_document_id - which is exactly what makes L03's 'no other revision' guarantee hold - is unverified here. I also could not verify the design's cross-repo obligations (the payload-hash baseline B-payload-hash remains non-executable).

The full product test suite was NOT run in the product repo. I ran the author's quoted 69-test set in the product repo, and the whole tests/contract directory only inside an isolated copy, which lacks docs/, AGENTS.md, README.md and some fixtures; its 45 pre-existing failures are environment artifacts of that copy, and I used them only as a baseline for the 2 additional failures caused by mutant M1b. No coverage measurement (--cov) and therefore no independent check of the FC-1204 coverage gate; .coverage/coverage.json were left untouched (git status --porcelain is empty).

The mutation experiments ran in temporary trees copied from the product repo; the product repo was never mutated, so each mutant's effect is measured against a copy that may differ from the product tree in untracked files (none that these four cases use). Python 3.13.9 / pytest 9.1.1 on this machine only.

F-B04-1's remedies were assessed by reading the design, file-scope and code, not by prototyping them; whether a canonical-writer snapshot is even feasible against immutable-raw conventions (companies/raw is read-only for this run) is a write-face question outside my access.

Out of scope: B05/B01/B03/B06/B07, the write face, the export/egress face, the worker face, the production .source_catalog state (deliberately untouched) and any R4 phase C/D work. I did not verify the claim that the four cases are 'F10 new tests only' against the owner's approval record beyond file-scope v0.1.7 section 1 (S-1 APPROVED, tests/contract new files only), which matches what the commit does.
I did not observe any network access: all probes ran locally under the repository's hermetic conftest (COMPANY_WIKI_NETWORK=blocked); no download or adapter path was exercised.
